data.description:
Altria (MO) operating company Helix Innovations announced Team Grass League as the winner of its inaugural on!vitational golf tournament.

Paige Spiranac and Team Grass League claimed golf’s orangest jacket following a dramatic comeback victory, with Flo Rida bringing the two-day event to an electrifying close with a hit-filled performance

RICHMOND, Va.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Helix Innovations LLC, an operating company of Altria Group, Inc. (Altria) (NYSE: MO), today announced the winners of on!® nicotine pouches’ inaugural on!vitational, held October 16 and 17 at TGL’s SoFi Center in Palm Beach Gardens, Florida. The two-day golf and entertainment experience brought together eight teams of current and former professional athletes, golf personalities, entertainers and adult nicotine consumers age 25+ for a competition that combined golf, technology and entertainment.

Well-known golf influencer Paige Spiranac and Team Grass League, including former professional golfer Drew Kittleson and Grass League co-founder Jimmy Hoselton, captured the inaugural on!vitational Championship. The team defeated former PGA TOUR veteran Ricky Barnes and Team Troon in a dramatic final to claim the tournament trophy and golf’s orangest jacket. After teams including Malbon, Palm Tree Crew and Hypegolf battled throughout the competition, Grass League staged a thrilling comeback, with an on!® consumer sweepstakes winner delivering a pivotal shot on the penultimate hole to help secure the victory.

Unlike traditional golf tournaments, the on!vitational put nicotine consumers 25+ directly into the competition alongside some of the biggest personalities in golf, sports and entertainment. Consumer participants, selected at random through an on!® sweepstakes earlier this year, competed as members of the eight teams. The two-day event was emceed by popular golf influencer and TGL host Roger Steele.

Grass League co-founder Jimmy Hoselton summed up the excitement: “on!® has been with us from the beginning. We're all in on on!®, and we're all in on the on!vitational.”

A New Kind of Golf Competition

Held inside TGL’s 250,000-square-foot SoFi Center, the on!vitational took advantage of the venue’s technology, including its over four-story tall simulator screen and real-life putting and short-game areas, to deliver a golf experience unlike a traditional tournament.

The competition also featured unique in-match opportunities. Momentum Swing allowed the sweepstakes winners to chip into designated round spots on the green for significant bonus points while Celeb Shot allowed teams to choose any team member to take a shot, regardless of whose turn it was. All Axis offered a strategic element where teams could move the green 45 or 90 degrees in any direction after their opponent was on or close to the green to gain short game and putting advantages at key moments.

These elements ended up being major factors in the final. Grass League was down 6-0 on No. 6. They used their Celeb Shot to allow Kittleson to hit, and he delivered. He chipped it in from off the green to give Grass League their first points of the match. A 20-foot birdie putt on No. 7 by Hoselton pulled Team Grass League within two points, and the Momentum Swing was the deciding factor. Trailing 6-4 on No. 8, Team Grass League sweepstakes winner William K. chipped it into one of the designated spots, scoring six points, and clinching the comeback Championship victory.

"This was one of the best experiences of my life," said on!® sweepstakes and Team Grass League winner William K. in a post-match interview. "My team kept picking me up throughout the tournament, and I was able to deliver when it counted. Really thankful to on!® for putting on such a great event."

Beyond the competition, multi-platinum recording artist Flo Rida headlined Saturday's entertainment, bringing an energy-filled conclusion to two great days of golf. He performed some of his biggest hits and invited tournament winners and guests to join him onstage.

Honoring Veterans Through Golf

The on!vitational also featured a partnership with the Veteran Golfers Association (VGA), a nonprofit dedicated to enriching the lives of veterans and their family members through the camaraderie and sportsmanship of golf.

In addition to competing as one of the tournament's eight teams, the VGA participated in a special military salute recognizing U.S. Navy veteran and Medal of Honor recipient Edward C. Byers Jr., who attended the event. All proceeds from can sales at the on!vitational went towards supporting the VGA and its mission.

Relive the on!vitational

Fans 21 or older can relive the competition, winning moments, player highlights and entertainment through content available on the on!® Instagram.

About on!® Nicotine Pouches

on!® and on! PLUS® nicotine pouches are designed for adult nicotine consumers 21+ looking for a satisfying, premium nicotine pouch experience. With six varieties and three nicotine strengths, on!® nicotine pouches deliver against a wide variety of adult consumer 21+ tastes and preferences. on! PLUS® nicotine pouches are designed with a proprietary NICOSILK™ mesh technology for a comfortable feel. on! PLUS® is available in Mint, Wintergreen & Tobacco flavors at 6, 9 and 12 mg strengths. on! PLUS® will also offer the same three strength options in exciting new flavors: Blueberry Mint, Mango Pineapple and Watermelon Mint (select stores only).

Helix Innovations LLC Profile

Helix Innovations LLC (Helix), an Altria company, offers a portfolio of oral nicotine pouch products for adult nicotine consumers 21+, including on!® and on! PLUS®. In December 2025, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration authorized the marketing of certain on! PLUS® variants.

Helix is committed to responsible marketing and preventing underage access to nicotine products. As an Altria operating company, Helix follows marketing practices designed to appeal to adult nicotine consumers 21+ while taking steps to limit reach to underage audiences.

No one under the age of 21 should use nicotine products. Nicotine is addictive, and nicotine products are not risk-free. on!® products are intended for adult nicotine consumers 21+.

data.description:

  • The 1-year graft failure-free survival at 12 months post-transplant was 90%, which is clinically meaningful
  • Graft and patient survival were 92% and 98%, respectively  
  • Idefirix was generally well tolerated with a safety profile consistent with previous clinical trial experience

LUND, Sweden, October 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Hansa Biopharma AB, "Hansa" (Nasdaq Stockholm: HNSA), today announced that data from the European Post-Authorization Efficacy and Safety (PAES) study of Idefirix® (imlifidase) were presented during the High-Impact Clinical Trials oral session at the American Society of Nephrology (ASN) Kidney Week 2026 in Denver, Colorado. The abstract "FR-OR103 Post-Authorization Efficacy and Safety (PAES): An Open-Label Post-Authorization Trial of 50 Imlifidase Crossmatch-Positive Deceased-Donor Kidney Transplants in Europe" was selected as a Late-Breaking Abstract at the congress.

Renée Aguiar-Lucander, CEO of Hansa Biopharma, said: "The presentation of the PAES study in the High-Impact Clinical Trials session highlights the scientific and clinical relevance of these findings and the potential of imlifidase to address a significant unmet need for highly sensitized patients awaiting kidney transplantation. We are encouraged by the continued interest from the transplant community in the growing body of evidence supporting imlifidase."

Oriol Bestard MD PhD, Vall d'Hebron University Hospital, Barcelona, Spain and investigator for the trial said: "The successful completion of the PAES study provides important evidence in a patient population that continues to face significant challenges in accessing kidney transplantation. These findings add to the clinical evidence supporting the use of imlifidase to enable transplantation in highly sensitized patients with a positive crossmatch against a deceased donor."

ASN Kidney Week is one of the world's leading scientific meetings in nephrology and transplantation, bringing together researchers and clinicians to present the latest advances in kidney disease and transplantation medicine. The High-Impact Clinical Trials session features selected studies considered to represent some of the most clinically relevant and impactful research presented at the congress.

The abstract was presented by Oriol Bestard MD PhD, Vall d'Hebron University Hospital, Barcelona, Spain, on behalf of the PAES study investigators.

Summary of the Abstract

Background

Imlifidase have a conditional approval in Europe since 2020. PAES (NCT05369975) is a controlled, non-randomized, open-label post-authorization efficacy and safety trial, designed to provide comprehensive data to support a full marketing authorisation of imlifidase (Idefirix®) in Europe.

Methods

Fifty highly sensitized (HS) patients who received crossmatch positive kidney offers received imlifidase treatment in line with the mode-of-action i.e. conversion of a positive crossmatch to a negative crossmatch and thereby enabling transplantation. All patients were unlikely to be transplanted under available kidney allocation systems, including prioritization programs for HS patients.

The primary trial objective was to assess graft failure-free survival at 1 year after transplantation. Secondary outcomes at 1 year includes kidney function assessed by eGFR, patient survival, graft survival, delayed graft function (DGF), antibody-mediated rejection (AMR) and safety.

Results

  • The graft failure-free survival was 90% at 1 year after transplantation in patients desensitized with imlifidase (n=50).
  • Graft and patient survival were 92% and 98%, respectively.
  • The mean eGFR calculated by MDRD was 51.04 mL/min/1.73 m2 (n=45).
  • DGF was seen in 40% of patients with a median duration of 14 days.
  • AMR occurred in 56% of recipients; however, no allograft loss was associated with AMR.
  • There were no new or additional safety signals found, and no imlifidase infusions were stopped due to infusion reactions.

Conclusion

Imlifidase enables kidney transplantation with a successful kidney function measured as eGFR at 1 year in patients desensitized. Imlifidase was well tolerated, with a safety profile consistent with prior experience and no unexpected or unacceptable risks observed.

Information about the trial is available at ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT05369975

Notes to editors

About highly sensitized patients

Highly sensitized patients have pre-formed antibodies with a broad reactivity against human leukocyte antigens (HLAs). Those antibodies can cause damage to a transplanted organ and potentially graft loss.1 The presence of HLA antibodies means that highly sensitized patients have limited or no access to transplantation, as finding a compatible donor organ 

is particularly challenging.2,3 The immunological complexity of highly sensitized patients make them spend a longer time on transplant waiting lists, with an increased risk of dying while waiting for a suitable donor organ.4,5 Across the U.S. and Europe, highly sensitized patients comprise around 10-15% of all patients on transplant waiting lists.6,7

About Idefirix® (imlifidase)

Imlifidase is an antibody-cleaving enzyme originating from Streptococcus pyogenes that specifically cleaves and inactivates all immunoglobulin G (IgG) antibody subclasses, including HLAs. It has a rapid onset and inactivates IgG-antibodies within hours after administration. The decrease in antibody levels creates a temporal antibody-free window of opportunity for highly sensitised patients to undergo transplant, thus enabling successful transplantation from an otherwise incompatible donor.

Imlifidase received a conditional marketing authorization valid throughout the European Union on 25 August 2020 and is marketed under the trade name Idefirix for the desensitization treatment of highly sensitized adult kidney transplant patients with a positive crossmatch against an available deceased donor. The use of Idefirix should be reserved for patients who are unlikely to be transplanted under the available kidney allocation system, including prioritization programs for highly sensitized patients.

The efficacy and safety of imlifidase as a pre-transplant treatment to reduce donor-specific IgG antibodies was studied in four phase 2 single-arm, studies in EU and US, a controlled Phase 3 study in US and in this European Post-Authorization Efficacy and Safety (PAES) study. 5,7,10-11 .

Full EU product information can be accessed via the initial Summary of Product Characteristics found here

Idefirix is exclusively out-licensed for transplantation in EU, UK, Switzerland, Norway, Liechtenstein, Iceland and Middle East and North Africa (MENA) to SERB Pharmaceuticals since July 1, 2026.

In the US, the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) accepted the Biologics License Application (BLA) for imlifidase in February of 2026 and assigned a Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) action date of December 19, 2026.

About kidney failure

Kidney disease can progress to kidney failure or End-Stage Renal Disease (ESRD), identified when a patient's kidney function is less than 15%.12 ESRD poses a significant health burden, affecting nearly 2.5 million patients worldwide.12 A kidney transplant is the treatment of choice for suitable patients with ESRD because it offers improved survival and quality of life benefits, and is cost savings compared to long-term dialysis. There are approximately 170,000 kidney patients in the U.S. and Europe waiting for a new kidney.13

About Hansa Biopharma

Hansa Biopharma AB is a pioneering commercial-stage biopharmaceutical company developing and commercializing novel immunomodulatory therapies to transform care for patients with acute or complex immune disorders. Hansa's proprietary IgG-cleaving enzyme technology platform addresses serious unmet medical needs in transplantation, gene therapy and autoimmune diseases. The company's portfolio includes imlifidase, a first-in-class immunoglobulin G (IgG) antibody-cleaving enzyme therapy, which has been shown to enable kidney transplantation in highly sensitized patients, and HNSA-5487, a next-generation IgG-cleaving molecule that will be developed for Guillain-Barré Syndrome (GBS). Hansa Biopharma is based in Lund, Sweden, and has operations in Europe and the U.S. The company is listed on Nasdaq Stockholm under the ticker HNSA. data.title: U.S. FDA Approves Subcutaneous Induction Regimen for AbbVie's SKYRIZI® (risankizumab-rzaa) for Adults With Moderately to Severely Active Crohn's Disease | ABBV Stock News
data.description:
The new regimen allows patients to begin SKYRIZI treatment at home rather than starting with intravenous administration.

See more from StockTitan in Google Search and AI answers.Adds StockTitan as a preferred source · opens Google
Add on Google
  • Now with a new route of induction administration, subcutaneous SKYRIZI supports early symptomatic and endoscopic control with an on-body injector (OBI) device throughout the course of treatment
  • In the pivotal Phase 3 AFFIRM study, subcutaneous (SC) SKYRIZI® achieved superior clinical remissioni and endoscopic responseii at week 12 compared with placebo in patients with Crohn's disease; results were particularly strong in patients without prior advanced therapy failureiii
  • The safety profile of subcutaneous induction was generally consistent with the established SKYRIZI profile in Crohn's disease, with no new safety risks identified
  • FDA also approved an update to the U.S. Prescribing Information warning and precautions across all indications to allow healthcare providers to use clinical judgment when determining whether tuberculosis (TB) testing is needed

NORTH CHICAGO, Ill., Oct. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- AbbVie (NYSE: ABBV) today announced the U.S. Food and Drug Administration has approved a subcutaneous (SC) induction regimen for SKYRIZI® (risankizumab-rzaa) for adults with moderately to severely active Crohn's disease (CD)iv. Patients now have the option to start SKYRIZI treatment at home, with induction doses delivered by an on-body injector (OBI) induction pack and then continue using an OBI once every eight weeks throughout the course of maintenance treatment.

"People living with Crohn's disease need treatments that can deliver meaningful disease control from the start," said Roopal Thakkar, M.D., executive vice president, research and development, chief scientific officer, AbbVie. "With the approval of subcutaneous induction, we are building on the strong efficacy of SKYRIZI while giving patients and physicians greater flexibility in how treatment is initiated. This is one more example of how AbbVie continues to advance treatment to better meet the needs of people living with Crohn's disease."

Subcutaneous SKYRIZI Shows High Rates of Clinical Remission and Endoscopic Response by Week 12iii 
This FDA approval is supported by positive results from the Phase 3 AFFIRM trial evaluating the efficacy and safety of SC SKYRIZI versus placebo in patients with moderately to severely active CD.iii SKYRIZI achieved superiority of the co-primary endpoints of clinical remission and endoscopic response at week 12.iii Although the study enrolled a primarily treatment-refractory population, these Phase 3 results were particularly strong within patients without prior advanced therapy failure (advanced therapy-naïve).iii By week 12, nearly three-quarters (74%) of advanced therapy (AT)-naïve patients were in clinical remission (vs. 27% placebo) and these AT-naïve patients achieved endoscopic response at four times the rate of placebo (60% vs. 15%, respectively).iii SC SKYRIZI also had a higher efficacy response in patients who had previously failed advanced therapy.iii

SC SKYRIZI also met secondary endpoints including endoscopic remission and FACIT fatigue scores at week 12 vs. placebo.iii The safety profile of SC SKYRIZI for induction was generally consistent with its known profile in CD, with no new safety risks observed.iii

Together, these results demonstrate market-leading clinical and endoscopic outcomes in advanced therapy-naïve patients that set a high bar in CD. Furthermore, the strength of these subcutaneous results provides a compelling foundation for future clinical trials.

Subcutaneous Treatment With SKYRIZI Offers Fully Self-Administered Therapy From the Start 
The induction dosing regimen with SC SKYRIZI is 720 mg delivered by OBI induction pack at weeks 0, 2, 4 and 8.iii Patients also have the option to start treatment intravenously with 600 mg delivered at weeks 0, 4 and 8.iii Patients can then continue with maintenance dosing starting at week 12 administered by OBI every eight weeks.iii

"When patients and I discuss treatment, they want to know two things: will it work? And how will it fit into their lives?" said Millie D. Long, M.D., MPH, chief, division of gastroenterology and hepatology, University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, and lead investigator of AFFIRM. "AFFIRM answered the first question, with superior rates of clinical remission and endoscopic response versus placebo during induction with subcutaneous SKYRIZI, particularly in patients new to advanced therapy. This approval answers the second. As a physician who has used the SKYRIZI OBI, I've seen firsthand the convenience it can offer patients. Now with this approval, patients can start treatment at home and continue the same way through maintenance."

Patients Report Satisfaction and Ease of Use in Real World Experience With SKYRIZI OBI
First introduced in 2022 for CD maintenance treatment, the SKYRIZI OBI has demonstrated strong user experience. In a real-world survey of 186 people living with CD, 88% reported AbbVie's OBI easy to use.v In evaluating alternative routes of administration, a patient-reported survey of 352 adults living with IBD found 87% were satisfied or highly satisfied with OBI compared to 71% with an autoinjectorvi, demonstrating patient preference for OBI.

FDA Also Approved Update to Tuberculosis (TB) Language in U.S. Prescribing Information
Additionally, the FDA approved an update to the SKYRIZI prescribing information's warning and precautions language across all approved indications.iii The revised label advises healthcare providers to consider TB evaluation prior to treatment initiation based on clinical judgment.iii This change gives healthcare providers greater flexibility in patient assessment before starting SKYRIZI treatment. There is no mandatory TB test prior to initiating SKYRIZI.

About Crohn's Disease 
Crohn's disease is a chronic, systemic disease that manifests as inflammation within the gastrointestinal tract, most commonly in the area between the small intestine (ileum) and the colon, causing persistent diarrhea and abdominal pain.vii,viii It is a progressive disease, meaning it gets worse over time and may lead to life-threatening complications or surgery.ix,x Because the signs and symptoms of Crohn's disease are unpredictable, it causes a significant burden on people living with the disease—not only physically but also emotionally and economically.xi

About the AFFIRM Studyxii
AFFIRM is a global, Phase 3, randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of risankizumab subcutaneous (SC) as an induction treatment in adult patients with moderately to severely active Crohn's disease. Co-primary endpoints were percentage of participants with CDAI Clinical Remission (CDAI < 150) and percentage of participants with endoscopic response at week 12. A total of 274 patients were randomized in a 2:1 ratio to risankizumab SC or placebo. Key demographics and baseline characteristics were generally balanced between the risankizumab SC and placebo groups; 65% had failed advanced therapies for the treatment of CD before. The study consists of three treatment periods: a placebo-controlled Period A (baseline to week 12) to evaluate the efficacy and safety of risankizumab SC induction treatment, an extended Period B (week 12 to 24) where patients receive blinded or open-label treatments based on their clinical response at week 12, and a 52-week open-label extension Period C where all patients receive the approved risankizumab maintenance treatment.xii More information on this trial can be found at www.clinicaltrials.gov (NCT06063967).xii

Patient Access and Support
AbbVie is committed to helping people access SKYRIZI and other medicines, including offering a patient support program and co-pay card that may reduce out-of-pocket costs to as little as $0 per month for eligible, commercially insured patients. For those with limited or no health insurance, AbbVie offers myAbbVie Assist, a patient assistance program that provides SKYRIZI at no charge to those who qualify. More information about this assistance program can be found at www.AbbVie.com/myAbbVieAssist.

About SKYRIZI® (risankizumab-rzaa)
SKYRIZI is an interleukin-23 (IL-23) inhibitor that blocks IL-23 by selectively binding to its p19 subunit. IL-23, a cytokine involved in inflammatory processes, is thought to be linked to a number of chronic immune-mediated diseases.iii SKYRIZI is approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for the treatment of moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis, plaque psoriasis, psoriatic arthritis and Crohn's disease.iii

SKYRIZI® (risankizumab-rzaa) U.S. Uses and Important Safety Informationiii
SKYRIZI is a prescription medicine used to treat:

  • moderate to severe plaque psoriasis in adults and children 6 years of age and older who may benefit from taking injections or pills (systemic therapy) or treatment using ultraviolet or UV light (phototherapy).
  • active psoriatic arthritis in adults and children 6 years of age and older.
  • moderately to severely active Crohn's disease in adults.
  • moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis in adults.

IMPORTANT SAFETY INFORMATION

What is the most important information I should know about SKYRIZI® (risankizumab-rzaa)?

SKYRIZI is a prescription medicine that may cause serious side effects, including:

Serious allergic reactions:

  • Stop using SKYRIZI and get emergency medical help right away if you get any of the following symptoms of a serious allergic reaction:
    • fainting, dizziness, feeling lightheaded (low blood pressure)
    • swelling of your face, eyelids, lips, mouth, tongue, or throat
    • trouble breathing or throat tightness
    • chest tightness
    • skin rash, hives
    • itching

Infections:
SKYRIZI may lower the ability of your immune system to fight infections and may increase your risk of infections. Your healthcare provider may check you for infections and tuberculosis (TB) before starting treatment with SKYRIZI and may treat you for TB before you begin treatment with SKYRIZI if you have a history of TB or have active TB. Your healthcare provider should watch you closely for signs and symptoms of TB during and after treatment with SKYRIZI.

  • Tell your healthcare provider right away if you have an infection or have symptoms of an infection, including:
    • fever, sweats, or chills
    • cough
    • shortness of breath
    • blood in your mucus (phlegm)
    • muscle aches
    • warm, red, or painful skin or sores on your body different from your psoriasis
    • weight loss
    • diarrhea or stomach pain
    • burning when you urinate or urinating more often than normal

Do not use SKYRIZI if you are allergic to risankizumab-rzaa or any of the ingredients in SKYRIZI. See the Medication Guide or Consumer Brief Summary for a complete list of ingredients.

Before using SKYRIZI, tell your healthcare provider about all of your medical conditions, including if you:

  • have any of the conditions or symptoms listed in the section "What is the most important information I should know about SKYRIZI?"
  • have an infection that does not go away or that keeps coming back.

Medications that interact with the immune system may increase your risk of getting an infection after receiving live vaccines. You should avoid receiving live vaccines right before, during, or right after treatment with SKYRIZI. Tell your healthcare provider that you are taking SKYRIZI before receiving a vaccine.
  • are pregnant or plan to become pregnant. It is not known if SKYRIZI can harm your unborn baby.

  • become pregnant while taking SKYRIZI. You are encouraged to enroll in the Pregnancy Registry, which is used to collect information about the health of you and your baby. Talk to your healthcare provider or call 1-877-302-2161 or visit http://glowpregnancyregistry.com to enroll in this registry.

Tell your healthcare provider about all the medicines you take, including prescription and over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, and herbal supplements.

SKYRIZI may cause serious side effects. See "What is the most important information I should know about SKYRIZI?"

Liver problems may happen while being treated for Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis: A person with Crohn's disease who received SKYRIZI through a vein in the arm developed changes in liver blood tests with a rash that led to hospitalization. Your healthcare provider will do blood tests to check your liver before, during, and at least up to 12 weeks of treatment, and may stop treatment with SKYRIZI if you develop liver problems. Tell your healthcare provider right away if you notice any of the following symptoms: unexplained rash, nausea, vomiting, stomach (abdominal) pain, tiredness (fatigue), loss of appetite, yellowing of the skin and eyes (jaundice), and dark urine.

The most common side effects of SKYRIZI in people treated for Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis include: upper respiratory infections, headache, joint pain, stomach (abdominal) pain, injection site reactions, low red blood cells (anemia), fever, back pain, urinary tract infection, and rash.

The most common side effects of SKYRIZI in people treated for plaque psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis include: upper respiratory infections, headache, feeling tired, injection site reactions, and fungal skin infections.

These are not all the possible side effects of SKYRIZI. Call your doctor for medical advice about side effects.

Use SKYRIZI exactly as your healthcare provider tells you to use it.

data.description:
Vertex plans an at-home autoinjector launch if povetacicept receives FDA approval.

See more from StockTitan in Google Search and AI answers.Adds StockTitan as a preferred source · opens Google
Add on Google

- Vertex is on track for the U.S. FDA Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) date of November 30 for potential accelerated approval of povetacicept –

- Data published in NEJM and presented at ASN highlight povetacicept’s unique trifecta of efficacy, favorable safety, and the simplicity of dosing at-home every 4 weeks with a low-volume autoinjector –

- Data presented at ASN include a qualitative study examining patient perspectives on current and emerging IgAN therapies, showing that 96% of participants preferred an autoinjector over a prefilled syringe, and 80% of participants preferred dosing every 4 weeks versus weekly dosing -

- New clinical studies of povetacicept underway including a study evaluating patient experience on povetacicept administered via autoinjector -

BOSTON--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Vertex Pharmaceuticals Incorporated (Nasdaq: VRTX) today announced the publication of Phase 3 RAINIER results for povetacicept in the New England Journal of Medicine (NEJM), presentation of these data at the American Society of Nephrology (ASN) Kidney Week 2026 in Denver, Colorado, and advancement of the povetacicept clinical research program in IgAN. Vertex will also host an investor event during ASN on October 23 at 6:15-7 p.m. MDT (8:15-9 p.m. EDT). Further details are below.

Data being presented include a pre-specified Week 36 interim analysis of the ongoing Phase 3 RAINIER trial of povetacicept, an engineered fusion protein and dual inhibitor of the BAFF (B cell activating factor) and APRIL (a proliferation inducing ligand) cytokines, in immunoglobulin A nephropathy (IgAN). RAINIER met its primary endpoint, with povetacicept achieving a 52.0% reduction from baseline in proteinuria at Week 36 and a statistically significant and clinically meaningful 49.8% reduction versus placebo (P<0.0001), while also meeting both secondary endpoints.

The Week 36 interim analysis of RAINIER demonstrated that the depth of proteinuria reduction from baseline was consistent across demographic, clinical and regional subgroups, including an unprecedented 54.2% reduction in urine protein to creatinine ratio (UPCR) versus placebo in North America. Additionally, findings showed that 42.2% of povetacicept-treated participants reached 24-hour UPCR <0.5 g/g, the threshold aligned with current Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) guidelines, compared with only 6.2% on placebo. Importantly, these findings were observed on top of optimized supportive care in both treatment arms, including sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitor use in 65.8% of participants, which is among the highest reported of any contemporary IgAN trial.

“At just 36 weeks of treatment, povetacicept has delivered impressive efficacy results, together with favorable safety and convenient dosing at-home every 4 weeks in a low-volume auto-injector that can fit into the lives of IgAN patients, underscoring the potential of povetacicept to substantially impact and redefine expectations for disease control in IgAN,” said Carmen Bozic, M.D., Executive Vice President, Global Medicines Development and Medical Affairs, and Chief Medical Officer at Vertex. “We are grateful to the patients, investigators, and study teams who made RAINIER the largest and fastest-enrolling contemporary IgAN trial to date and look forward to the November 30th PDUFA target action date.”

“What stands out from the RAINIER results is the important clinical validation of simultaneously targeting BAFF and APRIL to address upstream drivers and kidney injury in IgA nephropathy. Povetacicept was specifically designed as a high-potency, high-affinity TACI fusion protein with broad tissue distribution to deliver this dual inhibition in order to target upstream pathogenic immune complex production,” said Richard Lafayette, M.D., Professor of Medicine (Nephrology) at Stanford University Medical Center and RAINIER Steering Committee Co-Chair, who presented the data at ASN Kidney Week. “The results observed with povetacicept are among the most compelling I have seen in IgAN and highlight the potential of povetacicept to become an important new treatment option for patients living with this chronic progressive disease.”

Vertex also presented findings from a qualitative study examining patient perspectives on the device design and administration of current and emerging IgAN therapies, “Patient Perceptions of Injectable Therapies Among Adults with IgAN: A Qualitative Study” (#TH-PO0473). The study included in-depth, one-on-one interviews with 25 U.S. adults living with IgAN. Participants were shown pictures and short videos of the devices and asked to assess key treatment administration-related attributes. Findings showed that 96% of participants (24 of 25) preferred the characteristics of an autoinjector over a prefilled syringe, citing features such as the needle not being visible and elimination of manual needle insertion. Additionally, 80% of patients (20 of 25) preferred dosing every 4 weeks versus weekly dosing, with the top reasons being convenience and travel or time away from home considerations.

Vertex also announced a new clinical trial underway for povetacicept:

  • PAVANT IgAN Patient Experience Study (NCT07890909), A Phase 3b, Open-label, Single-arm, Patient Experience Study of Povetacicept Injection (via Autoinjector) in Adults With Immunoglobulin A Nephropathy

Visit news.vrtx.com/kidney-congress for more information about Vertex’s presence at ASN Kidney Week 2026.

Investor Event

Vertex will host an investor event and webcast on October 23 at 6:15-7 p.m. MDT (8:15-9 p.m. EDT) in Denver, Colorado, to discuss the data for povetacicept in IgAN, the Company’s program in APOL1- mediated kidney disease (AMKD), and other highlights across its kidney disease portfolio.

A live webcast of the presentation and Q&A portions can be accessed through the Investor Relations section of Vertex's website at investors.vrtx.com. To ensure a timely connection, it is recommended that participants register at least 15 minutes prior to the scheduled webcast. An archived webcast will be available on the company's website in the “Investors” section.

About RAINIER

RAINIER (NCT06564142) is a global Phase 3 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pivotal trial of povetacicept 80 mg administered subcutaneously every 4 weeks versus placebo on top of standard of care in 605 adults with IgAN (N=557 in main cohort, N=48 in the exploratory cohort). The trial was designed to have a pre-planned interim analysis evaluating the percent change from baseline in UPCR for the povetacicept arm versus placebo after a pre-specified number of patients reach 36 weeks of treatment. Final analysis will occur at two years of treatment, with a primary endpoint of total estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) slope through Week 104. RAINIER is the largest trial conducted in IgAN and achieved full enrollment faster than any contemporary IgAN trial.

As previously reported, patients treated with povetacicept achieved a 52.0% reduction from baseline in 24-hour UPCR at Week 36, with a statistically significant and clinically meaningful reduction of 49.8% in 24-hour UPCR compared to placebo (P<0.0001).

The trial also met its secondary objective. For the first secondary endpoint, patients treated with povetacicept demonstrated a 77.4% reduction from baseline in serum galactose deficient IgA1 (Gd-IgA1) compared to an increase of +9.1% in the placebo group, yielding a reduction of 79.3% compared to placebo (P<0.0001). For the second secondary endpoint, in patients with baseline hematuria, 85.1% achieved hematuria resolution in the povetacicept treatment group compared to 23.4% in the placebo group, resulting in hematuria resolution of 61.7% compared to placebo (P<0.0001).

Povetacicept was generally safe and well tolerated. The majority of adverse events (AEs) were mild to moderate. The most common events (≥10% of participants in either treatment group) for the povetacicept group versus the placebo group were upper respiratory tract infection (18.3% vs 11.4%), nasopharyngitis (9.7% vs 12.4%), and injection site reactions (14.5% vs 2.2%). There were no serious adverse events (SAEs) related to povetacicept and no deaths in the trial. There were no opportunistic infections, and no discontinuations due to infections. As expected, anti-drug antibodies (ADAs) were observed; these ADAs had no impact on efficacy or the risk profile.

Results from the RAINIER trial support the Biologics License Application (BLA) for povetacicept, which has been accepted by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for accelerated approval in adults with IgAN. The Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) target action date is November 30, 2026.

The RAINIER trial continues in a blinded manner until the last patient enrolled completes 104 weeks. Patients in RAINIER who have completed the Week 104 visit are eligible to enroll in the open-label extension study (NCT07807995), “A Phase 3 Open-Label Study of Long-term Treatment With Povetacicept in Adults With Immunoglobulin A Nephropathy,” and receive an additional 104 weeks of treatment and follow-up.

About Povetacicept

Povetacicept is a dual inhibitor of the BAFF and APRIL cytokines, which promote B cell activation, differentiation and/or survival, and provides B cell control by inhibiting the ability of BAFF and APRIL to drive the pathogenesis of multiple immune-mediated diseases. Due to its engineered TACI domain, povetacicept has demonstrated improved binding affinity, potency, pharmacokinetics, and/or tissue distribution compared to other APRIL, BAFF, and dual BAFF+APRIL inhibitors in preclinical studies.

If povetacicept is approved by the FDA, Vertex plans to launch povetacicept as a low-volume (<0.5 mL) subcutaneous autoinjector delivered once every 4 weeks via at-home administration.

IgAN is the first of multiple indications that Vertex is exploring for povetacicept given its pipeline-in-a-product potential. There are ongoing studies including the Phase 2/3 OLYMPUS trial (NCT07204275) in primary membranous nephropathy (pMN) and the Phase 2 ETNA trial (NCT07501702) in generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG).

About IgA Nephropathy (IgAN)

IgAN is a serious, progressive, life-threatening kidney disease driven by uncontrolled autoreactive B cell activity and is the most common cause of primary glomerulonephritis, affecting approximately 330,000 people in the United States and Europe and more than 1.5 million globally. IgAN results from the deposition of circulating immune complexes, consisting of immunoglobulins and galactose-deficient immunoglobulin A (Gd-IgA1), in the renal glomerular mesangium, triggering kidney injury and fibrosis.

About Vertex

Vertex is a global biotechnology company that invests in scientific innovation to create transformative medicines for people with serious diseases and conditions. The company has approved therapies for cystic fibrosis, sickle cell disease, transfusion-dependent beta thalassemia, acute pain and acromegaly, and it continues to advance clinical and research programs in these areas. Vertex also has a robust clinical pipeline of investigational therapies across a range of modalities in other serious diseases where it has deep insight into causal human biology, including IgA nephropathy, neuropathic pain, APOL1-mediated kidney disease, primary membranous nephropathy, congenital adrenal hyperplasia, adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH)-dependent Cushing's syndrome, autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease, type 1 diabetes, generalized myasthenia gravis, and myotonic dystrophy type 1.

Vertex was founded in 1989 and has its global headquarters in Boston, with international headquarters in London. Additionally, the company has research and development sites and commercial offices in North America, Europe, Australia, Latin America and the Middle East. CARLSBAD, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Ionis Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (Nasdaq: IONS) partner Roche announced today late-breaking oral presentation data from the ongoing Phase 3 IMAgINATION study in adults with primary IgA nephropathy (IgAN) receiving optimized standard of care, demonstrating that investigational sefaxersen achieved a statistically significant and clinically meaningful 43.1% reduction in proteinuria (95% confidence interval [CI]: 32.5 - 52.0, P<0.0001), relative to placebo at 37 weeks, as measured by 24-hour urine protein-to-creatinine ratio (UPCR). Proteinuria is a key indicator of kidney damage and a reduction in UPCR is strongly associated with the preservation of long-term kidney function. Results presented at the American Society of Nephrology (ASN) Kidney Week 2026 also showed that, among patients with baseline hematuria (blood in urine), a greater proportion of patients achieved hematuria resolution at Week 37 with sefaxersen versus placebo.

"These data support our belief that sefaxersen is uniquely positioned to treat IgA nephropathy, demonstrating significant and clinically meaningful reduction in proteinuria and offering the potential to help reduce the need for long-term dialysis or kidney transplantation,” said Brett P. Monia, Ph.D., chief executive officer, Ionis. “Sefaxersen is a powerful example of the broad impact of Ionis' innovative science, and based on these results, we believe it has the potential to be an important new treatment option for people living with IgA nephropathy."

The treatment effect in all prespecified subgroups was consistent with the clinically meaningful reductions in proteinuria shown in the primary endpoint results. Sefaxersen was well tolerated with a safety profile consistent with the previously reported Phase 2 study, exhibiting no new safety signals.

Sefaxersen is an investigational once-monthly subcutaneous injection designed to enable self-administration for people with IgAN. The IMAgINATION study will continue as a blinded study to evaluate the change in kidney function over two years, as measured by estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) at week 105. Roche will share data with health authorities, with the goal of bringing this treatment to patients as soon as possible.

Typically diagnosed before the age of 40, IgAN affects at least 25 adults per million worldwide each year. Roche licensed sefaxersen from Ionis for the treatment of complement-mediated diseases. About sefaxersen

Sefaxersen, an investigational, highly specific liver-directed antisense oligonucleotide that inhibits factor B production, is the first RNA-targeted therapy for IgA nephropathy (IgAN). Serum complement factor B levels are elevated in people with IgAN. Sefaxersen is designed to provide sustained control of the alternative complement pathway, an important pathway in IgAN, enabling once-monthly subcutaneous dosing and is intended for self-administration in people with IgAN.

About the IMAgINATION Study

IMAgINATION (NCT05797610) is a Phase 3, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of subcutaneous sefaxersen, an investigational antisense inhibitor of complement factor B, in patients with primary IgA nephropathy at high risk of progression. The study enrolled 459 people, who are randomized 1:1 to receive sefaxersen or placebo for 105 weeks. Participants may switch to open-label treatment after week 105 at the investigator's discretion or after the common-close timepoint, whichever occurs first. The primary endpoint of the study is the change from baseline in the urine protein-to-creatinine ratio at 37 weeks.

About IgA Nephropathy (IgAN)

IgAN, also known as Berger’s disease, is a serious, chronic and progressive autoimmune kidney disease affecting at least 25 adults per million worldwide each year and is typically diagnosed before the age of 40 years. In IgAN, immune complexes deposit in the kidneys, which activates the complement system’s alternative pathway, leading to inflammation and subsequent kidney damage. It is the most common form of primary glomerulonephritis (inflammation of kidney glomeruli) and remains a leading cause of kidney failure, with up to 50% of patients experiencing end-stage kidney disease within 20 years of diagnosis. Many current therapies aim to reduce protein levels in the urine and control blood pressure to slow progression of the disease.

Updated KDIGO 2025 guidelines* highlight the need to address both the underlying immune-mediated causes of IgAN and the downstream consequences of kidney damage. While new therapies have expanded treatment options, important unmet needs remain, including improved long-term preservation of kidney function and more targeted approaches that address key drivers of disease progression.

The interim proteinuria result precedes the ongoing study’s evaluation of kidney-function change at week 105.

- Sefaxersen achieved a statistically significant 43.1% reduction in proteinuria, a key indicator of kidney damage, relative to placebo at 37 weeks with consistent treatment effects across all prespecified patient subgroups -

- As the first antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) evaluated in IgAN, sefaxersen inhibits complement factor B production and has the potential to slow IgAN disease progression by reducing kidney inflammation -

- Investigational sefaxersen is intended to be a once-monthly subcutaneous injection and designed to enable convenient self-administration at home -

- Despite recent advances, many people with IgAN remain at risk of disease progression and kidney failure, highlighting the need for additional targeted treatment options for those who do not respond to initial therapy -

SOUTH SAN FRANCISCO, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Genentech, a member of the Roche Group (SIX: RO, ROP; OTCQX: RHHBY), announced today late-breaking oral presentation data from the ongoing Phase III IMAgINATION study in adults with primary IgA nephropathy (IgAN) receiving optimized standard of care, demonstrating that investigational sefaxersen achieved a statistically significant and clinically meaningful 43.1% reduction in proteinuria (95% confidence interval [CI]: 32.5 - 52.0, P<0.0001), relative to placebo at 37 weeks, as measured by 24-hour urine protein-to-creatinine ratio (UPCR). Proteinuria is a key indicator of kidney damage and a reduction in UPCR is strongly associated with the preservation of long-term kidney function. Results presented at the American Society of Nephrology (ASN) Kidney Week 2026 also showed that, among patients with baseline hematuria (blood in urine), a greater proportion of patients achieved hematuria resolution at Week 37 with sefaxersen versus placebo.

“These Phase III results demonstrate the potential for sefaxersen to meaningfully reduce protein in the urine, a key indicator of kidney damage, in people with IgA nephropathy,” said Levi Garraway, M.D., Ph.D., chief medical officer and head of Global Product Development. “By inhibiting complement factor B in the liver, sefaxersen may offer a novel approach to slow disease progression in IgAN, potentially helping patients delay or avoid long-term dialysis or kidney transplantation.”

The treatment effect in all prespecified subgroups was consistent with the clinically meaningful reductions in proteinuria shown in the primary endpoint results. Sefaxersen was well tolerated with a safety profile consistent with the previously reported Phase II study, exhibiting no new safety signals.

Sefaxersen is an investigational once-monthly subcutaneous injection designed to enable convenient self-administration for people with IgAN. The IMAgINATION study will continue as a blinded study to evaluate the change in kidney function over two years, as measured by estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) at week 105. Data will be shared with health authorities, with the goal of bringing this treatment to patients as soon as possible.

Typically diagnosed before the age of 40, IgAN affects at least 25 adults per million worldwide each year. IgAN, also known as Berger’s disease, is a chronic and progressive autoimmune disease that leads to end-stage kidney disease in up to 50% of patients within 20 years of diagnosis. It is the most common form of primary glomerulonephritis (inflammation of the tiny filters, glomeruli, in the kidneys) and is a major cause of chronic kidney disease as well as kidney failure.

About sefaxersen

Investigational sefaxersen is the first highly specific liver-directed antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) inhibitor of factor B production being evaluated in IgA nephropathy (IgAN). Serum complement factor B levels are elevated in people with IgAN. When we reduce these levels, it in turn reduces the level of protein in urine, which is a key indicator of improved kidney function.

Sefaxersen is designed to provide sustained control of the alternative complement pathway, an important pathway in IgAN, enabling once-monthly subcutaneous dosing and is intended for self-administration in people with IgAN. In Phase I and II trials, sefaxersen was shown to be generally well tolerated in healthy volunteers and people with IgAN who were at high risk of progression, and reduced proteinuria and plasma complement factor B.

Roche licensed sefaxersen from Ionis Pharmaceuticals for the treatment of complement mediated diseases.

About the IMAgINATION Study

IMAgINATION [NCT05797610] is a Phase III, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of subcutaneous sefaxersen, an investigational antisense inhibitor of complement factor B, in patients with primary IgA nephropathy at high risk of progression. The study enrolled 459 people, who are randomized 1:1 to receive sefaxersen or placebo for 105 weeks. Participants may switch to open-label treatment after week 105 at the investigator’s discretion or after the common-close timepoint, whichever occurs first. The primary endpoint of the study is the change from baseline in the urine protein-to-creatinine ratio at 37 weeks.

About primary immunoglobulin A nephropathy (IgAN)

IgAN, also known as Berger’s disease, is a serious, chronic and progressive autoimmune kidney disease affecting at least 25 adults per million worldwide each year and is typically diagnosed before the age of 40 years. In IgAN, immune complexes deposit in the kidneys, which activates the complement system’s alternative pathway, leading to inflammation and subsequent kidney damage. It is the most common form of primary glomerulonephritis (inflammation of kidney glomeruli) and remains a leading cause of kidney failure, with up to 50% of patients experiencing end-stage kidney disease within 20 years of diagnosis. Many current therapies aim to reduce protein levels in the urine and control blood pressure to slow progression of the disease.

Updated KDIGO 2025 guidelines* highlight the need to address both the underlying immune-mediated causes of IgAN and the downstream consequences of kidney damage. While new therapies have expanded treatment options, important unmet needs remain, including improved long-term preservation of kidney function and more targeted approaches that address key drivers of disease progression.

About Genentech in Immunology

Genentech is committed to harnessing pioneering science and innovation to address critical unmet needs for patients with immune-mediated diseases. Our pipeline includes over a dozen clinical programs in immunology aiming to transform care for people living with lupus, MASH, ulcerative colitis, Crohn’s disease, immunoglobulin A nephropathy, idiopathic nephrotic syndrome, and rheumatoid arthritis. We are investing end-to-end in immunology from discovery to R&D to commercialization across a variety of modalities including monoclonal antibodies, bispecifics, and CAR-T cell therapies to help solve some of the most difficult challenges in immunology today.

About Genentech

Founded 50 years ago, Genentech is a leading biotechnology company that discovers, develops, manufactures and commercializes medicines to treat patients with serious and life-threatening medical conditions. The company, a member of the Roche Group, has headquarters in South San Francisco, California. For additional information about the company, please visit http://www.gene.com.
